assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's single curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit: YOO_JINHO_CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md (status active_provisional), read in full, including its evidence discipline, executive model, speech architecture, psychological architecture, decision engine, relationship-conditioned registers, developmental states, primary-source anchor map, simulation rules, confidence matrix, open questions and falsification tests. It is repository analysis of the Chugong Korean novel omnibus (main story, side stories 1-21 and two postscripts) with manhwa evidence excluded. The model's own A rating and the project entrypoint's description are inputs, not conclusions. The numbered synthesis documents it uses as retrieval maps, the other Solo Leveling character models and capability records, and the primary text are not curated on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. No primary-source inspection was made.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Yoo Jinho from his first C-rank raid and the Dongsuk betrayal (index_split_001) through the guild-license request (index_split_002), family gathering and dinner with Yoo Myunghan (index_split_004, 007), perceived avoidance (index_split_008), Ahjin office administration (index_split_014), Hwang Dongsoo torture and rescue (index_split_024, 025), the international business introduction (index_split_025), to the reset-world proposal and family conversations (index_split_032) as endpoint. States follow the model's five-stage sequence; the reset-world adult does not carry the original raid history. Locators are omnibus split files, so a state change inside one file cannot be placed more finely.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model states a core need (to be valued as himself apart from wealth, family name and other people's power), six invariants (visible attachment; fear that does not decide the final choice; a fairness instinct; money as a language of capability and affection; desire for earned recognition; deference that does not erase personhood) and a six-step decision engine conditioned on who is present, whether he understands the domain, whether someone is treated unfairly, whether he is afraid and what loyalty requires, whether he feels unable to prove worth, and whether a trusted person has recognized his competence. It also predicts his errors: overidealizing Jinwoo, catastrophizing ambiguous relational signals (the perceived-avoidance drinking scene, index_split_008), early overconfidence relative to experience (index_split_001) and material overcompensation when insecure (index_split_032). Not B: most rules rest on one or two summarized scenes cited only at omnibus-file granularity, without quotation or paragraph anchor, and the model's own V2 falsification tests remain open on core rules: whether status ever outranks fairness in unsampled scenes, whether his business competence depends on others doing the work, and whether loyalty eliminates independent judgment. The evidence states the discriminating account but does not yet establish it. Not D: the account is explicit, operational and conditioned rather than a description of distributed traits.

Five developmental states are named with their concerns and the simulation errors to avoid: inexperienced D-rank beginner, guild-license aspirant, Ahjin formation and vice-master apprenticeship, post-torture chosen brother, and reset-world adult. The reset-world state is used as evidence that business aptitude, expressiveness and the need to prove worth are not artifacts of hunter society. Not B: states are located only by omnibus split file (index_split_001 to index_split_032), with no chapter or paragraph boundary, so a state change inside a file cannot be placed. Not D: the states are ordered and separately characterized.

The model gives a relationship-conditioned register account: socially active, affectively permeable baseline with short bursts, questions, repetition and emotional particles; 형 moving to the stable, deferential but intimate 형님 with Jinwoo; formal address and a weaker voice with his father; concise, respectful applied reasoning in the contract dispute; polished executive mode at the international business introduction; and contraction to the vulgar two-syllable 좆까 under Hwang Dongsoo's torture. Not B: apart from 형, 형님 and 좆까, no Korean strings are quoted, the model says full hand-coded register analysis and dialogue attribution are still pending, and its stylometric scan is explicitly unvalidated. Not D: register shifts are tied to named addressees and situations.

Ordinary conduct is described across states: filling silence and pushing toward contact on the first raid, asking permission to leave a family gathering, drinking and distress over a perceived avoidance, low alcohol tolerance, extravagant gift planning and attempted hugs in the reset-world proposal conversation, and family talk about Cha and Suho. The decision engine's worth-insecurity step gives a conditional account of when material gestures or ordinary presence become likely. Not B: these windows are summarized without quotations or fine locators, and behavior with unrelated close friends is rated medium-low by the model. Not D: a conditional rule for low-stakes behavior is given and supported in more than one state.

The relationship-conditioned registers give partner-specific deltas that the anchor map ties to contrasting scenes: Jinwoo (형님, deferential grammar with high familiarity, sensitivity to perceived avoidance, competence when work is delegated; index_split_001, 002, 008, 014, 025, 032), his father Yoo Myunghan (formal address, weaker voice, careful requests, narrated courage to ask to be entrusted with Yoojin Guild; index_split_004 and 007), family peers and cousins, business counterparts (index_split_025), hostile stronger actors (Hwang Dongsoo, index_split_024) and Jinah (CB). The father-versus-Jinwoo contrast is observed within one scene (index_split_004), not inferred. Not A: Jinah, cousins and unrelated friends are thin and the model marks romance medium and unrelated intimate friends medium-low. Not C: the conditioning is explicit, partner-specific and recurrent in the dominant relations.

The model reconstructs his inner motive (proving worth apart from wealth and the better-positioned older brother) and attachment system from narrated inhibition before his father, his stated reasons in the contract dispute and his emotional overflow after rescue, and labels the home-environment explanation as strong inference (SI). Not B: inner states are inferred from conduct and a few narrated moments, without located interior passages. Not D: the inference is explicit and labeled by claim type.

Conflict conduct is described with a rule: fear appears first, then loyalty, fairness or self-respect decides. Anchors are the first-raid contract challenge to senior hunters, standing beside the apparently E-rank Jinwoo during the Dongsuk betrayal, confronting his father, and refusing a false accusation through repeated torture with minimal defiant speech (index_split_001, 007, 024). He defers on elite combat strategy beyond his rank. Not B: physical combat is barely characterized beyond fear and endurance, and each conflict type rests on one summarized scene. Not D: the separation of emotional state from choice is stated as a rule across several scenes.

Practical values are clear (fairness in a concrete deal, refusal to lie or sell out someone he has accepted, honesty with his father about Jinwoo's help), but the model rates abstract political philosophy low-medium and says systematic ideology is not strongly textualized; no deliberation between competing goods is analyzed. Not C: the evidence gives positions and loyalties rather than reasoned weighing. Not E: the fairness and loyalty choices recur across states.

The model gives a source of his comedy (sincerity rather than deliberate wit: overenthusiasm, literal grand gestures, status incongruity, transparent emotion), a located diagnostic exchange (the first-raid joke that he has never had to live watching other people's reactions, index_split_001), ordinary joking about Cha and Suho (index_split_032), and a use rule (comedy works when he means what he says; not a constant joke machine). Not B: humor is not conditioned by partner beyond Jinwoo and family. Not D: an explicit account and use rule are supported across states.

The model's corpus is the complete Chugong Korean novel omnibus including side stories 1-21 and two postscripts, with manhwa excluded, and it reports whole-novel search followed by concentrated close reading of thirteen anchor scenes. Not C: anchors are omnibus split files, not chapters or paragraphs, dialogue attribution was not hand-validated, and the model lists paragraph-level anchoring of the torture and proposal sequences as pending. Not E: every developmental state has at least one analyzed anchor.

Affirmative limits are stated with reasons: fear is not cowardice and emotional transparency is not shallowness; loyalty is voluntary and not shadow-like submission; money is not his deepest value; adult maturation does not reduce expressiveness; elaborate heroic speeches under torture are not supported; profanity belongs only to an extreme boundary; everyday romantic speech with Jinah is not to be over-specified. Not B: several limits rest on the model's interpretation of single scenes, and its own falsification tests could overturn three of them. Not D: each limit is stated as a rule tied to an anchor.

The five states are ordered, and the reset-world state is explicitly separated from the original raid history. Not C: anchors are split-file locators shared by several scenes (index_split_001 holds three anchors, index_split_025 and 032 two each), there are no chapter numbers, and no knowledge-locality or probe freeze is defined. Not E: the state sequence is explicit and used in the simulation rules.

conditions: Output is illustrative, never attributed quotation, and names one developmental state.

The addressee is Jinwoo, Yoo Myunghan, a business counterpart or a hostile stronger actor, in the register the model gives for that relation; dialogue with Jinah, cousins or unrelated friends is not generated beyond the model's CB.
Korean address follows the model (형 early, 형님 as stable mature address; formal address with his father); no casual same-age address to Jinwoo and no constant 형님 gag without content.
Manhwa dialogue is not reconstructed from this evidence.
scenario_readiness.note: Under the owner rulings the question is whether the evidence constrains output enough for the declared use. For illustrative speech to Jinwoo, his father or a business counterpart it does at the level of address, register and content rules (형님-centered vertical warmth, inhibition with his father, concise competence in a familiar domain, terse defiance only at a moral breaking point). The lack of quoted strings and validated attribution limits exact wording and is carried by the conditions.

conditions: Chronology is one named developmental state; reset-world Jinho does not carry the original raid history.
The interlocutor is Jinwoo, his father, a business counterpart, a hostile stronger actor or a stranger in an unfair deal; transfer to other partners is lower confidence.
The setting is a raid, a contract or guild-administration matter, a family occasion or a business meeting, with his rank, his competence in the domain and any coercion stated.
Output predicts priorities and likely choices, including visible fear, overidealization and material overcompensation, not exact speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named state: D-rank beginner, guild-license aspirant, Ahjin formation, post-torture chosen brother, or reset-world adult, stated explicitly.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Jinwoo as 형님, his father as intimidating evaluator, a business counterpart, a hostile stronger actor, or a stranger in an unfair deal, in the relation the model gives.
setting_constraints: Raid, contract or guild administration, family occasion, or business meeting
Rank, domain competence and any coercion stated
No romantic or unrelated-friend scenario beyond the model's CB; no manhwa-only material

scenario_readiness.note: The decision engine and portable card support bounded transfer when the scenario supplies what the engine asks for: who is present and what relation he wants to preserve, whether he knows the domain, whether someone is treated unfairly, and what loyalty would require if self-protection were easier.

conditions: The setting is low-stakes contact with Jinwoo, Jinwoo's family or his own family, with the state named.
Output keeps high expressivity (questions, reassurance-seeking, gushing, attempted physical affection) and treats material gestures as proof-seeking or affection, not greed.
Everyday life with Jinah and with unrelated friends is not specified.
scenario_readiness.note: Supported by the first-raid contact behavior, family-gathering and perceived-avoidance scenes, and the reset-world proposal and family conversations, with the worth-insecurity rule for gifts versus ordinary presence.

The evidence supports his practical loyalty and fairness choices, which are covered under cross-scenario and conflict claims, but the model says systematic ideology is not strongly textualized and analyzes no weighing of competing goods. A dilemma that turns on reasoning rather than on loyalty or a concrete unfairness is not supported.

The model gives adult commitment, proposal anxiety, extravagant planning and advice-seeking from Jinwoo, but marks everyday romantic speech with Jinah as a confidence boundary and rates the romance medium with limited everyday interaction. Romantic interaction itself is not reconstructable from this evidence.

conditions: The setting is a contract, guild administration, legal or logistical matter, or a business representation, with his role and state named.
Output gives him real competence, polite presentation and visible pleasure at Jinwoo's validation, and defers on elite combat strategy beyond his rank.
The model's open falsification test on whether his business competence depends on others' substantive work is stated as a limit; detailed corporate strategy is not predicted.
scenario_readiness.note: Supported by the first-raid contract dispute, Ahjin office administration and legal complaints (index_split_014), the international business introduction (index_split_025) and reset-world management under his father, with the model's rule that clarity rises and stammering falls in a domain he understands.

known_limits.statement: The model rates itself A, robust for speech, psychology and behavior in most contexts, while keeping active_provisional status until its V2 validation; that rating is an input, not this assessment's tier.

The model lists open V2 falsification tests on core rules: status over fairness in unsampled scenes, business competence that depends on others' work, loyalty that eliminates independent judgment, adult reduction of expressiveness, and grand gestures as status display. Until they are run, those rules are hypotheses the evidence supports but has not tested.

Anchors are omnibus split files (index_split_001 to index_split_032), several of which hold more than one anchor scene; there are no chapter or paragraph locators, and the model lists paragraph-level anchoring of the torture and proposal sequences as pending.
Jinho-attributed dialogue has not been hand-validated; the several-hundred-turn scan is explicitly not validated stylometry, and only 형, 형님 and 좆까 are quoted.

Fear is expected to appear first and not to decide the final choice when loyalty or fairness is at stake (first raid, father dinner, Hwang torture); a reconstruction neither removes the fear nor converts it into cool heroism.
The terse vulgar refusal under torture belongs to an extreme moral boundary that strips social accommodation; it is not his ordinary anger register.
Reset-world adult Jinho lacks the original raid history; development and personality recur, but memories of Ahjin, the torture and the rescue are not his in that state.
Everyday romantic interaction with Jinah is a stated confidence boundary in the model.
The model excludes manhwa evidence, so no claim here covers the manhwa incarnation or its dialogue.

The numbered Solo Leveling synthesis documents the model uses as retrieval maps, and the primary text itself, are not curated evidence on this subject; their support for the model's scene summaries was not checked here.
Behavior with unrelated intimate friends and political reasoning are rated medium-low and low-medium by the model; the evidence set does not establish them.
